sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Pankaj Dwivedi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 152 of 2022, under sections 420, 467, 468 IPC, Police Station- Iradat Nagar, District- Agra.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that he is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

In this case, overloaded truck was challaned by R.T.O. and it was brought to the police station but the driver fled away regarding which case under Section 3/5 of Prevention of Damages to Public Property Act was registered.

opennyai_summary.facts: This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 152 of 2022, under sections 420, 467, 468 IPC, Police Station- Iradat Nagar, District- Agra.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In this case, overloaded truck was challaned by R.T.O. and it was brought to the police station but the driver fled away regarding which case under Section 3/5 of Prevention of Damages to Public Property Act was registered.
Applicant is crusher owner who is said to have issued e-pass in back date though this allegation is false because e-pass was issued online.
1 applicant has been involved in several cases by the police out of which in those cases, he has been granted anticipatory bail by co-ordinate Bench of this Court.
Since investigation is going on,
therefore, he is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, he is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., the perusal of record and without commenting on the merits of the case, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Raj Kumar Khandelwal, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report, if any, under section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police office as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
